newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche's Breuer says relieved at steel agreement.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche's Breuer says relieved at steel agreement.

text.p: Rolf Breuer, designated future chief executive of Germany's Deutsche Bank AG, said on Monday he welcomed the peaceful resolution to the now aborted takeover battle in the German steel industry.

Denying that any party had been forced to capitulate, Breuer said in a television interview that Krupp AG's decision to shelve its hostile bid in favour of a merger with Thyssen AG "fills me with great relief."

After a week of escalating public protest over the takeover bid and five days of talks, Krupp and Thyssen said they planned to found a steel joint venture and explore expanding their co-operation into other areas.

The agreement rendered void Krupp's takeover bid for Thyssen, which it launched last week to the horror of steel workers and many politicians, who accused banks of Wild West tactics in backing the takeover plan.
Breuer said the saga had ended "not so differently from many initially hostile bids in the U.S. or U.K".
But he also said significant job cuts would still be inevitable in the steel sector.

"I think this is a need of which all participants have been aware for years. The German steel sector is simply not internationally competitive ... from Thyssen or Krupp it costs more than from British Steel," Breuer said.
Breuer rejected charges that Deutsche Bank had behaved inappropriately in supporting Krupp's takeover bid in the first place.
"We are mediators, we are advisors," he said. "If an industrial client has a project, we will investigate it."
